research_question: In women with early-stage triple-negative breast cancer, does adding platinum-based chemotherapy (carboplatin or cisplatin) to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, compared with the same neoadjuvant chemotherapy without platinum, improve disease-free survival?
treatment_label: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with added platinum (carboplatin or cisplatin)
outcome_description: Disease-free survival (including event-free survival, relapse-free survival, or invasive disease-free survival when DFS is not reported; DFS preferred when both are available), extracted as the reported hazard ratio with its 95% confidence interval for the platinum arm versus the platinum-free control arm, using the longest follow-up reported. The 95% CI is converted to a standard error of the log hazard ratio; HRs reported as control versus platinum are inverted (HR to 1/HR with the interval swapped). Hazard ratios are not reconstructed from event counts or Kaplan-Meier curves.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges g (equivalently, a hazard ratio below 1) means longer disease-free survival in the platinum-containing neoadjuvant arm — i.e. fewer recurrence/progression/death events — favouring the addition of platinum.
search_queries: neoadjuvant carboplatin triple-negative breast cancer randomized trial disease-free survival
platinum neoadjuvant chemotherapy triple negative breast cancer event-free survival long-term outcome
cisplatin preoperative chemotherapy triple-negative breast cancer randomised controlled trial recurrence hazard ratio
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial of neoadjuvant (pre-operative) chemotherapy in patients with early-stage triple-negative breast cancer (or a TNBC subgroup reported separately)
Compares a platinum-containing arm (carboplatin or cisplatin) with an otherwise comparable platinum-free control arm
Reports a hazard ratio with 95% confidence interval (or equivalent quantitative survival estimate) for disease-free, event-free, relapse-free, or invasive disease-free survival
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, narrative review, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between a platinum-containing treatment arm and a platinum-free control condition (single-arm studies, or trials in which all arms receive platinum)

No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed — no reported hazard ratio with 95% CI (or equivalent); e.g. only Kaplan-Meier curves and numbers at risk, or only pathological complete response data

Unrelated to the research topic — platinum given only in the adjuvant (post-operative) setting or mixing neoadjuvant and adjuvant platinum, populations restricted to HER2-positive breast cancer, metastatic/advanced disease, or other cancers
moderators_to_extract: Backbone regimen (anthracycline/taxane-containing vs taxane-only vs other) and platinum dosing schedule (weekly vs 3-weekly)
Sample size / number of randomised TNBC patients
Survival endpoint definition used (DFS vs EFS vs RFS vs iDFS)
Trial region/multicentre status and BRCA mutation status proportion
effect_size_note: Pool log hazard ratios with inverse-variance weighting under a fixed-effect model (random-effects as fallback if fixed-effect is unavailable). SE(log HR) = (ln(upper CI) − ln(lower CI)) / 3.92. HR < 1 favours platinum. Invert HRs reported as control versus platinum. For trials with two platinum arms sharing a single control group, include each platinum-vs-control comparison separately and flag the shared control for sensitivity analysis. Use the longest-follow-up long-term survival analysis when multiple reports exist for the same trial, and avoid double-counting duplicate publications of the same trial.
